facts.statement: Tralkasaurus is a genus of abelisaurid dinosaur from the Huincul Formation in Río Negro Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: Tralkasaurus (meaning "thunder lizard") is a genus of abelisaurid dinosaur from the Huincul Formation from Río Negro Province in Argentina.

facts.statement: Tralkasaurus is a medium-sized abelisaurid with a mix of traits from early-diverging forms and the specialized Brachyrostra clade, making its exact classification uncertain.
facts.quote: A medium-sized abelisaurid, Tralkasaurus exhibits a conflicting blend of characteristics found among the early-diverging abelisauroids with others that characterize the highly specialized clade Brachyrostra, and thus its position within the clade is poorly-resolved.

facts.statement: The fossil site containing Tralkasaurus was discovered in 1999 by Sebastián Apesteguía near the village of El Cuy in Argentina.
facts.quote: The Violante Farm fossil site in Río Negro Province, Argentina, near the village of El Cuy, was discovered in 1999 by Sebastián Apesteguía on the north shore of the Ezequiel Ramos Mexía Reservoir.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MPCA-Pv 815 consists of an incomplete skeleton including a maxilla, various vertebrae, ribs, and a poorly preserved pubis.
facts.quote: The specimens discovered included an incomplete skeleton of an abelisaurid, catalogued as MPCA-Pv 815, which comprises a maxilla; dorsal, sacral, and caudal vertebrae; cervical ribs; and a badly-preserved pubis.

facts.statement: The name Tralkasaurus combines the Mapudungun word for thunder with the Greek word for lizard, while the species name refers to the discovery village of El Cuy.
facts.quote: The generic name is formed from "tralka", the Mapudungun word for "thunder", and the suffix -saurus, meaning lizard, while the specific name refers to the village of El Cuy.

facts.statement: Tralkasaurus had a maxilla measuring 22 cm, which is smaller than the 32 cm maxilla of the similarly sized dinosaur Skorpiovenator.
facts.quote: Its maxilla has a length of 22 cm, smaller than that of the similarly "medium-sized" Skorpiovenator (at 32 cm, with the whole animal measuring 6 m long).

facts.statement: Tralkasaurus is unique among abelisaurids for having the front margin of its antorbital fenestra slope forwards and upwards.
facts.quote: Tralkasaurus is unique among abelisaurids in that front margin of the antorbital fenestra slopes forwards and upwards, instead of being vertical or sloping backwards.

facts.statement: The maxilla of Tralkasaurus contained eleven tooth sockets, of which four teeth were preserved.
facts.quote: The maxilla also bears eleven sockets with four preserved teeth, which are typical of abelisaurids.

facts.statement: Unlike Skorpiovenator, Tralkasaurus possessed teeth where the serrations on both edges were the same size, similar to Majungasaurus.
facts.quote: Like Majungasaurus but unlike Skorpiovenator, the serrations on both edges of the teeth are the same size.

facts.statement: Tralkasaurus had forward and backward projecting processes on its tail vertebrae that overlapped, a trait characteristic of the Brachyrostra clade.
facts.quote: Processes projecting forwards and backwards at their tips would have been overlapping between caudal vertebrae; this is a distinguishing characteristic of the Brachyrostra.

facts.statement: Tralkasaurus shares key abelisaurid traits including a deep maxilla, fused interdental plates, specific vertebral connections, inclined tail processes, and a thin pubic shaft.
facts.quote: They found that it possesses synapomorphies of the Abelisauridae: a maxilla with a deep body, low ascending process, and reduced maxillary fossa, covered by foramina and rugosities; fused interdental plates lining the inside of the maxillary tooth row bearing strong vertical ridges; the subdivision of the infradiapophyseal fossae by the posterior paradiapophyseal laminae; a connection between the transverse processes and parapophyses by the dorsal paradiapophyseal laminae; large transverse processes strongly inclined upwards on the caudal vertebrae; and a thin pubic shaft.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Tralkasaurus among basal abelisaurids but fails to resolve its exact relationship to other species due to conflicting traits.
facts.quote: The phylogenetic analysis accordingly placed Tralkasaurus among basal abelisaurids, but was unable to resolve its affinities beyond a polytomy (collapsed tree).

facts.statement: Tralkasaurus lived in the Albian stage of the Early Cretaceous, as indicated by the volcanic ash-bearing sandstones of the Huincul Formation.
facts.quote: The strata exposed are yellowish and greenish sandstones that are occasionally tuffaceous (i.e. bearing volcanic ash), which belong to the Albian Huincul Formation.

facts.statement: Tralkasaurus lived in what is now South America, specifically in the Huincul Formation of Argentina.
facts.quote: Fue descubierto en la Formación Huincul de la Provincia de Río Negro, Argentina y descrito por Cerroni et al., 2020.

facts.statement: Tralkasaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 97 to 93 million years ago, spanning the Cenomanian to Turonian stages.
facts.quote: vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente de 97 a 93 millones de años, durante el Cenomaniano al Turoniano

facts.statement: Tralkasaurus coexisted with titanosaurian sauropods and an ornithopod in the Huincul Formation ecosystem.
facts.quote: Other dinosaurs also include a titanosaurian sauropod and an ornithopod.

facts.statement: The name Tralkasaurus cuyi translates to "thunder lizard of El Cuy," referencing the Mapudungun word for thunder and the discovery village.
facts.quote: Tralkasaurus cuyi ("lagarto trueno de El Cuy", ya que tralka es "trueno" en mapudungun y cuyi es en referencia a El Cuy, el pueblo en que fue descubierto)

facts.statement: The fossil site "Rancho Violante" near El Cuy in Río Negro province, Argentina, was discovered in 1999 by Sebastián Apesteguía.
facts.quote: El sitio de fósiles "Rancho Violante" en la provincia de Río Negro, Argentina, cerca del pueblo de El Cuy, fue descubierto en 1999 por Sebastián Apesteguía en la costa norte del Embalse Ezequiel Ramos Mexía.

facts.statement: Tralkasaurus was formally described in 2020 by Mauricio Cerroni et al.
facts.quote: El abelisáurido fue descrito formalmente en 2020 por Mauricio Cerroni et al. como Tralkasaurus cuyi

facts.statement: The generic name Tralkasaurus is derived from the Mapudungun word "tralka" for "thunder" and the suffix "-saurus" meaning "lizard".
facts.quote: el nombre genérico se forma a partir de "tralka", la palabra mapudungun para "trueno", y el sufijo -saurus, que significa lagarto

facts.statement: Tralkasaurus is described as a medium-sized abelisaurid.
facts.quote: Tralkasaurus fue descrito por Cerroni et al. como un "abelisáurido de tamaño mediano".

facts.statement: The maxilla of Tralkasaurus measures 22 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: Su maxilar tiene una longitud de 22 centímetros (8,7 pulgadas)

facts.statement: The complete animal measured 6 meters in length.
facts.quote: con el animal completo midiendo 6 metros (20 pies) de largo

facts.statement: The pubis of Tralkasaurus measures 35 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: el pubis de Tralkasaurus que mide 35 centímetros (14 pulgadas) de largo

facts.statement: The maxilla is a subtriangular bone covered in neurovascular foramina and rugosities.
facts.quote: El maxilar de Tralkasaurus es un hueso subtriangular cubierto de agujeros neurovasculares (hoyos formados por inervación) y rugosidades (áreas rugosas).

facts.statement: Tralkasaurus is unique among abelisaurids for having the front margin of the antorbital fenestra incline forward and upward.
facts.quote: Tralkasaurus es único entre los abelisáuridos en que el margen frontal de la fenestra antorbital se inclina hacia adelante y hacia arriba

facts.statement: The maxilla possesses eleven alveoli with four preserved teeth.
facts.quote: El maxilar también tiene once alvéolos con cuatro dientes conservados

facts.statement: The striations on both edges of the teeth are of the same size.
facts.quote: las estrías en ambos bordes de los dientes son del mismo tamaño

facts.statement: The transverse processes projecting outward and downward are distinctive among abelisaurids due to their unusual narrowness and shortness.
facts.quote: las parapófisis que se proyectan hacia afuera y hacia abajo son distintivas entre los abelisáuridos por su inusual estrechez y brevedad

facts.statement: Processes projecting forward and backward at the tips of the caudal vertebrae would have overlapped, a distinctive feature of Brachyrostra.
facts.quote: Los procesos que se proyectan hacia adelante y hacia atrás en sus puntas se habrían superpuesto entre las vértebras caudales; esta es una característica distintiva de los Brachyrostra.

facts.statement: Cerroni et al. performed a phylogenetic analysis to determine the affinities of Tralkasaurus.
facts.quote: Cerroni et al. realizaron un análisis filogenético para determinar las afinidades de Tralkasaurus.

facts.statement: The forward-inclined front margin of the antorbital fenestra, rod-shaped parapophyses, and low paradiapophyseal laminae are identified as autapomorphies of Tralkasaurus.
facts.quote: También identificaron el margen frontal inclinado hacia adelante de la fenestra antorbital y su excavación del cuerpo del maxilar, las parapofisis en forma de varilla y las láminas paradiapofisarias bajas como autapomorfias de Tralkasaurus.

facts.statement: Tralkasaurus exhibits a conflicting combination of features, with caudal transverse process projections typical of Brachyrostra but extensive antorbital fossae that are plesiomorphic like basal abelisauroids.
facts.quote: En particular, exhibe una combinación conflictiva de características: las proyecciones en los procesos transversales caudales son típicos de los Brachyrostra, pero la presencia de extensas fosas antorbitarias en el maxilar es plesiomórfica (es decir, característica de los abelisauroideos basales y a diferencia de otros abelisáuridos).

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis placed Tralkasaurus as a basal abelisaurid but could not resolve its affinities beyond a polytomy.
facts.quote: En consecuencia, el análisis filogenético colocó a Tralkasaurus como un abelisáurido basal, pero no pudo resolver sus afinidades más allá de una politomía (árbol colapsado).

facts.statement: The fossils belong to the Cenomanian-Turonian age of the Huincul Formation.
facts.quote: que pertenecen a la Formación Huincul del Cenomaniano-Turoniano.

facts.statement: Tralkasaurus lived during the Albian stage, between 110.1 and 106.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (110.1 to 106.3 million years ago)

facts.statement: Numerous theropods are known from Rancho Violante, including Gualicho, Aoniraptor, Taurovenator, an unenlagine, and an unnamed carcarodontosaurid.
facts.quote: Se conocen numerosos terópodos del Rancho Violante, incluidos Gualicho y Aoniraptor,que pueden representar o no el mismo megaraptórido, el carcarodontosáurido Taurovenator, un celurosaurio, identificado por Cerroni et al. como un unenlagino y otro carcarodontosáurido que permanece sin nombre, pero probablemente distinto al anterior y otro megaraptórido indeterminado.

facts.statement: Other dinosaurs found in the area include a titanosaurian sauropod and an ornithopod.
facts.quote: Otros dinosaurios también incluyen un saurópodo titanosauriano y un ornitópodo.
